text: Why is it faster? Here is an energy profile for this reaction: energy up the side, the progress of the reaction along the bottom. The substrate starts here; the product ends here, in this example a little lower; and in between there is a hill. To react, the substrate has to get over that hill, and its height is the activation energy, the energy that has to be put in before the reaction can go. The enzyme lowers the activation energy: same start, same finish, a lower hill. The gap between the two peaks is the reduction, not either hill on its own. A lower hill means many more molecules get over it in a given time, so the rate goes up.
